subject.title: fix(gateway): reap stale MCP processes on session reset regardless of…

question: Which lifecycle contract should gate MCP runtime retirement during reset/delete timeouts?
rationale: The stale-process bug needs a fix, but immediate pre-drain disposal can break active MCP work; choosing force-clear semantics versus lease-deferred retirement is maintainer lifecycle policy, not a safe mechanical edit.

options.title: Repair the lifecycle contract first
options.body: Require the PR to retire MCP runtimes only after drain, force-clear, or lease-aware deferred disposal, with reset/delete timeout tests before merge.

options.title: Require stronger proof before choosing
options.body: Ask for redacted live gateway logs or terminal output from an active-MCP reset/delete timeout before deciding whether this ordering is acceptable.

options.title: Pause for broader MCP runtime work
options.body: Pause or close this branch if maintainers want the stale-process cluster solved through a broader atomic lease/deferred-retirement runtime design.

recommendation.title: Repair the lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Require the PR to retire MCP runtimes only after drain, force-clear, or lease-aware deferred disposal, with reset/delete timeout tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the current assignee and already supplied the clearest related lifecycle-safety decision in this MCP cleanup cluster.
